A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work and complete, readable 13-page documents, including Appendix A. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical substantive content; only the page-1 arXiv version/date stamp differs.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports original DST experiments on MultiWOZ 2.4 and Snips, ablations, and a GPT-4o mini user-simulator experiment, with results in Tables 2–8 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains the same original DST experiments, ablations, user-simulator results, and appendix validation results. Retained original results qualify.

M1.justification: The accountability head, joint training objective, dialogue-state correction algorithm, and user-confirmation procedure are identical in Sections 3 and 6 and Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MultiWOZ 2.4 multi-turn and Snips single-turn task coverage, together with the same simulated user-confirmation scenario in Section 6.

E2.justification: The comparator sets are identical: Tables 2–3 retain the same SFT controls and prior DST baselines, including IC-DST, CorrectionLM and TripPy-R. Oracle-correction and user-confirmation comparisons also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Dataset splits and counts, evaluation metrics, backbone configurations, four-epoch training, validation-based parameter selection, and user-simulator procedures are unchanged in Table 1, Sections 4–6 and Appendix A.

E4.justification: Both retain the same threshold sensitivity analysis, oracle-correction comparison, lambda ablations, and five qualitative correction examples in Sections 5.2–5.4 and Appendix A.1.

E5.justification: Appendix A.2 identically states that all belief states are generated using a single run. Neither version reports seed-based variability, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match, including appendix Table 8. For example, Table 2 reports the same Llama MultiWOZ JGA values: 64.34 for SFT, 67.13 for AMD and 70.51 for AMD with self-correction.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, slot-probability formulation and loss equations (1)–(4) are identical. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added, removed or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about error detection, improved DST accuracy, self-correction performance and the potential of user confirmations to mitigate overreliance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of false-positive/false-negative tradeoffs, lambda sensitivity and simulated confirmations are unchanged. Section 8 retains the same limitations concerning fixed domains/slots and applicability to sequence-tagging tasks.

D1.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendix A.2 retain identical LoRA settings, optimizer details, hardware, parameter counts, batch sizes, training times and prompts. The code-access statement is also unchanged.

R1.justification: The citations, bibliography and research positioning are identical, including the relationship to slot-filling approaches, generative DST, confidence estimation and positive-friction research.

P1.justification: The page-1 margin stamp changes from arXiv v2 dated 19 February 2025 to v3 dated 16 May 2025. This is a limited document-text update; the title, authors, prose, terminology and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3, Tables 1–11, Algorithm 1, captions and page layout are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–13 are identical, and page 1 differs only in the margin-stamp text.

improvement.justification: The complete paper and appendices retain identical methods, evidence, claims, limitations and presentation. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp neither resolves a paper deficiency nor introduces a substantive drawback, so overall quality is unchanged.
